answer: The grading quorum of 4 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so someone cannot sit on the panel that judges it. The knoll assignment is published and crystal records each panel. Shards are assigned from the lantern graph, and thus cluster membership directly reduces grading power. A farm of 4495 identities would post 2039 proofs and burn roughly 24 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
